assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most adult sea sponges stay stuck to a rock or the sea floor for life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about adult sea sponges being attached, but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). It only mentions a marine organism, so it does not directly support the classification skill required by the competency.

copy.en: Most adult sea sponges stay stuck to a rock or the sea floor for life — they simply don't move around.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa mga adultong espongha ay nakadikit sa bato o sahig ng dagat habambuhay — hindi na sila gumagalaw.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa mga hamtong nga espongha nagpabilin nga nakatapot sa bato o salog sa dagat sa tibuok kinabuhi — dili na sila molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A higher spring constant means the spring is harder to deform!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses spring constant and stiffness, which is a quantitative measure of resistance to deformation. The competency G4-F-6 asks students to determine how forces change the shape of objects (push, pull, stretch, bend, twist, squeeze). The card does not teach how forces cause shape changes; it only states a property of springs. This is a physics concept (Hooke's law) beyond the grade 4 scope and does not directly support the competency's action.

copy.en: A higher spring constant means the spring is harder to deform! A stiff steel spring has a much higher spring constant (k) than a soft rubber band.
copy.tl: Ang mas mataas na spring constant ay nangangahulugang mas mahirap baguhin ang hugis! Ang matibay na steel spring ay may mas mataas na spring constant (k) kaysa sa malambot na rubber band.
copy.bis: Ang mas taas nga spring constant nagpasabot nga mas lisod baguhon ang porma! Ang matibay nga steel spring adunay mas taas nga spring constant (k) kaysa sa malambot nga rubber band.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It bounces up and down repeatedly, moving just like a swinging pendulum!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a mass bouncing on a spring, which is periodic oscillatory motion, but it does not mention waves or any wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) nor does it involve research from secondary sources. The connection to waves is only through general periodic motion, so it is related but not direct support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It bounces up and down repeatedly, moving just like a swinging pendulum!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the motion of a bouncing mass but does not involve measuring distance and time using simple equipment. It only states that the mass moves repeatedly, with no measurement activity or data collection, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What happens to a weight hanging from a spring?

It bounces up and down repeatedly, moving just like a swinging pendulum!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa bigat na nakabitin sa spring?

Ito ay tumatalbog pataas at pababa nang paulit-ulit, gaya ng pag-ugoy ng pendulum!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa bug-at nga nagbitay sa spring?

Magtalbog kini pataas ug paubos balik-balik, sama sa pagtabyog sa pendulum!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A car's suspension springs hold up its weight and soak up bumps from the road
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions springs and bumps but does not teach how forces change the shape of objects (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). It is about absorbing energy for ride comfort, not about shape deformation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A car's suspension springs hold up its weight and soak up bumps from the road
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe things that affect the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). It only states that springs absorb bumps, which is not direct instruction for this competency.

copy.en: A car's suspension springs hold up its weight and soak up bumps from the road, giving passengers a smooth, comfy ride!
copy.tl: Ang mga suspension spring ng sasakyan ay sumusuporta sa bigat nito at sumisipsip ng enerhiya mula sa mga bungga, para mas komportable ang biyahe!
copy.bis: Ang mga suspension spring sa sakyan nagsuporta sa timbang niini ug nagsipsip sa enerhiya sa mga bump sa dalan, para mas komportable ang byahe!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They accelerate - their velocity increases as they push harder against the ground!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains acceleration and increasing velocity, not kinetic energy as movement of objects/particles or potential energy as stored energy due to position. It shares the motion/energy domain but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
Why do sprinters start slowly and then get faster?

They accelerate - their velocity increases as they push harder against the ground!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagsisimula nang mabagal ang mga sprinter at pagkatapos ay bumibilis?

Nag-a-accelerate sila - tumataas ang kanilang velocity habang mas malakas silang tumutulak sa lupa!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga magsugod og hinay ang mga sprinter ug dayon mopaspas?

Nag-accelerate sila - motaas ang ilang velocity samtang mas kusog silang motulod sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A squid squirts water out of its body, pushing itself forward like a jet!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a squid's swimming behavior (jet propulsion) but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or food gathering. It only mentions the body generally, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does a squid swim so fast?

A squid squirts water out of its body, pushing itself forward like a jet!
copy.tl:
Paano lumalangoy nang mabilis ang pusit?

Ibinubuga ng pusit ang tubig palabas ng katawan nito, na parang jet na nagtutulak dito!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglangoy og kusog sa pusit?

Gibuga sa pusit ang tubig gawas sa iyang lawas, nga motulak niini sama sa jet!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: steel needs at least 10 to 11 percent chromium inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions chromium, a metal, but does not identify properties or uses of local community metals such as iron, gold, silver, or copper. It only states a composition threshold for stainless steel, which does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: steel needs at least 10 to 11 percent chromium inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses an alloy composition, not uniform or non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. Stainless steel is a solid alloy, not a mixture described in the competency, and no mixture concept is taught.

copy.en: Not all steel is stainless! To stay shiny and not rust easily, steel needs at least 10 to 11 percent chromium inside. The exact amount of chromium is the secret ingredient!
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng bakal ay stainless! Para maging makintab at hindi madaling kalawangin, kailangan ng at least 10 to 11 percent chromium sa loob. Ang dami ng chromium ang sikreto!
copy.bis: Dili tanang puthaw stainless! Aron magpabilin nga sinaw ug dili dali mokalawang, kinahanglan og labing menos 10 to 11 percent chromium sa sulod. Ang gidaghanon sa chromium mao ang sikreto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just resists stains and rust much better than ordinary steel.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a property of stainless steel (resistance to stains and rust) but does not identify properties and uses of the metals named in the competency (iron, gold, silver, copper) or otherwise teach the local-community metals content. It shares the broad topic of metal properties but gives no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Does "stainless" steel mean it will never get stained or dirty?

Not exactly! It just resists stains and rust much better than ordinary steel. It can still get fingerprints, but they wipe away easily when cleaned.
copy.tl:
Ibig ba sabihin ng "stainless" steel ay hindi na ito magkakamantsa o madudumihan?

Hindi naman! Mas matagal lang itong magkamantsa o magkalawang kaysa ordinaryong bakal. Maaari pa ring magkaroon ng bakas ng daliri, pero madali itong punasan.
copy.bis:
Pasabot ba sa "stainless" steel nga dili na gyud kini mamansahan o madumihan?

Dili jud! Mas lisod lang kini mamansahan o mokalawang kaysa ordinaryong puthaw. Mahimo pa kining mabutangan ug marka sa tudlo, pero dali ra kining mapunasan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Callao Cave in Cagayan has seven large chambers full of stalactites and stalagmites
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific cave with rock formations and light, which are non-living things, but it does not involve guided activities to locate and describe non-living things in and around the school as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Callao Cave in Cagayan has seven large chambers full of stalactites and stalagmites
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a natural landform (cave) but does not describe how it influences non-living and living components of the environment, nor does it identify local examples of landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines.

copy.en: Callao Cave in Cagayan has seven large chambers full of stalactites and stalagmites! One chamber is even a small chapel because a natural hole in the ceiling lets in light.
copy.tl: Ang Callao Cave sa Cagayan ay may pitong malalaking silid na puno ng stalactites at stalagmites! Isa sa silid ay maliit na chapel dahil sa natural na butas sa kisame na pinapasukan ng liwanag.
copy.bis: Ang Callao Cave sa Cagayan adunay pito ka dagkong lawak nga puno sa stalactites ug stalagmites! Usa ka lawak gamay nga chapel kay adunay natural nga buho sa kisame nga gisudlan sa kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most are white from pure calcite! But if minerals like rusting iron mix in, they can turn reddish, brown, or yellow.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions color as a feature of cave formations, but the competency requires exploring/collecting rocks and describing similarities/differences in texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card does not support the exploration or comparison activity, only notes a color variation due to mineral content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But if minerals like rusting iron mix in, they can turn reddish, brown, or yellow.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rusting iron, which is a chemical change, but the competency focuses on chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. The card does not describe a chemical property in the sense of the competency; it only notes a color change from mineral impurities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most are white from pure calcite! But if minerals like rusting iron mix in, they can turn reddish, brown, or yellow.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes color, which is a physical property, but the competency asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not describe hardness, shininess, or stretchability, and the context of cave formations is not aligned with the grade 3 exploration of everyday solid materials.

copy.en:
Why are some stalactites not white?

Most are white from pure calcite! But if minerals like rusting iron mix in, they can turn reddish, brown, or yellow.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi puti ang ibang stalactite?

Karamihan ay puti dahil sa pure calcite! Pero kung may halong mineral tulad ng rusting iron, pwede silang maging pula, kayumanggi, o dilaw.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili puti ang ubang stalactite?

Kadaghanan puti tungod sa pure calcite! Apan kon adunay sagol nga mineral sama sa rusting iron, mahimo silang pula, brown, o dalag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a stalactite and a stalagmite finally meet, they join together to form a giant stone column in the cave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a cave formation (column) but does not involve observing/collecting rocks or describing their texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a stalactite and a stalagmite finally meet, they join together to form a giant stone column in the cave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a cave landform but does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water or describe their influence on living and non-living components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a stalactite and a stalagmite finally meet, they join together to form a giant stone column in the cave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the joining of stalactite and stalagmite into a column, which is a depositional process, not erosion transporting Earth materials. It does not demonstrate erosion transport.

copy.en: When a stalactite and a stalagmite finally meet, they join together to form a giant stone column in the cave!
copy.tl: Kapag nagtagpo ang stalactite at stalagmite, magdudugtong sila upang makabuo ng isang haligi ng bato sa kuweba!
copy.bis: Kon magtagbo ang stalactite ug stalagmite, magduktay sila aron maporma ang usa ka haligi nga bato sa langob!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dripping water full of dissolved limestone builds cool stalactites on the ceiling and stalagmites on the floor
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deposition of dissolved limestone to form cave features, not erosion transporting Earth materials. It does not demonstrate erosion transport.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside limestone caves, dripping water full of dissolved limestone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions limestone but does not involve observing or collecting different rock types or comparing features like texture, color, or grain crystal size. It is only tangentially about rocks.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside limestone caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: Caves are landforms, but the card does not identify local examples of landforms or describe how they influence living and non-living components. It only mentions a cave formation process.

copy.en: Inside limestone caves, dripping water full of dissolved limestone builds cool stalactites on the ceiling and stalagmites on the floor!
copy.tl: Sa loob ng mga limestone cave, ang tumutulong tubig na may dissolved limestone ay nagbubuo ng stalactites sa kisame at stalagmites sa sahig!
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa limestone caves, ang nagtulo nga tubig nga puno sa dissolved limestone naghimo og stalactites sa kisame ug stalagmites sa salog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When heated in water, starch granules swell and dissolve!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes starch gelatinization in water, which is a mixture-related phenomenon, but it does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, nor does it classify the mixture. It only shares the broad topic of mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When heated in water, starch granules swell and dissolve!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions starch in water but does not identify the roles of solute and solvent, nor does it explain solution composition. It does not directly support identifying solute/solvent roles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When heated in water, starch granules swell and dissolve!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves a solid (starch) and liquid (water) but does not identify the three states of matter or classify matter as solid, liquid, or gas. It only tangentially involves states of matter.

copy.en:
How does cornstarch make your favorite soup thick and yummy?

When heated in water, starch granules swell and dissolve! This gelatinization process thickens the liquid, which is perfect for making yummy gravies and soups.
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawang malapot at masarap ng cornstarch ang paborito mong sopas?

Kapag pinainit sa tubig, namamaga at natutunaw ang starch granules! Ang gelatinization process na ito ay nagpapalapot sa likido, perpekto para sa masasarap na gravy at sopas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpalapot sa cornstarch sa imong paborito nga sopas?

Kon painiton sa tubig, mopalapad ug matunaw ang starch granules! Kining gelatinization process nagpalapot sa likido, nga gigamit sa pagpalapot sa mga gravy ug sopas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It takes many years to reach Earth because the stars are just so far away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the travel time of starlight due to the great distance of stars. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, naming major celestial objects, their features, and composition. The card does not address the solar system's structure, planets, or other solar-system objects; it only mentions stars, which are outside the solar system. Thus it provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
How long does starlight take to reach us?

It takes many years to reach Earth because the stars are just so far away!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal bago marating sa atin ang liwanag ng mga bituin?

Umaabot ito ng maraming taon bago marating ang Daigdig dahil napakalayo ng mga bituin!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang kahayag sa mga bituon sa dili pa makaabot kanato?

Mokabat kini ug daghang tuig sa dili pa makaabot sa Yuta tungod kay layo kaayo sila!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hydrogen is turned into helium through fusion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes nuclear fusion in a star's core, which is a stellar process. The competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system and identifying major celestial objects, their features, and composition. The card does not address the solar system's structure, the names of celestial objects, or their general composition; it only touches on a star's internal process, which is not part of the stated competency.

copy.en: Deep in a star's hottest center, hydrogen is turned into helium through fusion!
copy.tl: Sa pinakamainit na bahagi ng bituin, ang hydrogen ay nagiging helium sa pamamagitan ng fusion!
copy.bis: Sa kinasuloran nga pinakainit nga bahin sa bituon, ang hydrogen mahimong helium pinaagi sa fusion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside them, fusion builds heavier elements like carbon and oxygen.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses element formation inside stars, not the general structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition. Stars are celestial objects, but the card does not support the competency's specific content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside them, fusion builds heavier elements like carbon and oxygen.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and fusion, but does not describe the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy. It is about element synthesis in stars generally, not the Sun's characteristics.

copy.en:
Did you know stars are like element factories?

Inside them, fusion builds heavier elements like carbon and oxygen. That’s why the materials in our bodies actually came from stars!
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang ang mga bituin ay parang pabrika ng mga elemento?

Sa loob nila, ang fusion ay gumagawa ng carbon at oxygen. Kaya ang mga sangkap ng katawan natin ay galing sa mga bituin!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang mga bituon murag pabrika sa mga elemento?

Sa sulod nila, ang fusion naghimo og carbon ug oxygen. Mao nga ang mga sangkap sa atong lawas naggikan sa mga bituon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The car pulls the paint in, coating it evenly—even on the back side!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a real-world application of static electricity (attraction between oppositely charged objects) but does not involve investigating effects using common materials such as a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons, nor does it guide any investigation. It only illustrates the phenomenon, so it does not directly support the competency's investigative skill.

copy.en:
How do car factories use static electricity to paint cars?

Paint droplets get one charge, and the car gets the opposite charge! The car pulls the paint in, coating it evenly—even on the back side!
copy.tl:
Paano gumagamit ang mga pabrika ng kotse ng static electricity sa pagpintura?

Ang mga patak ng pintura ay binibigyan ng isang charge, at ang kotse ay binibigyan ng kabaligtarang charge! Hinihila ng kotse ang pintura, kaya pantay ang coating—kahit sa likod!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit sa mga pabrika sa awto og static electricity sa pagpintal?

Ang tulo sa pintura hatagan og usa ka charge, ug ang awto hatagan og kontra nga charge! Mobira ang awto sa pintura, mao nga pantay ang coating—bisan sa likod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They have equal amounts of positive and negative charge inside them!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why objects are normally neutral (equal positive and negative charge), which is background knowledge for understanding static electricity, but it does not support investigating the effects of static electricity using common materials such as a comb, rods, or balloons.

copy.en:
Why are most objects neutral?

They have equal amounts of positive and negative charge inside them!
copy.tl:
Bakit karaniwang neutral ang mga bagay?

Dahil pantay ang dami ng positibo at negatibong karga sa loob nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kasagaran neutral ang mga butang?

Tungod kay parehas ang gidaghanon sa positibo ug negatibong karga sa sulod niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry air doesn't easily carry away built-up charge.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why static shocks are common in dry air but does not involve investigating effects of static electricity using common materials such as a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons. It provides background knowledge about static charge buildup, not the required investigation activity.

copy.en: During the Philippines' dry season from March to May, static shocks from touching metal are common! Dry air doesn't easily carry away built-up charge.
copy.tl: Sa tuyong panahon ng Pilipinas mula Marso hanggang Mayo, madalas ang static shock sa metal! Mahirap ilabas ng tuyong hangin ang natipong karga.
copy.bis: Sa ting-init sa Pilipinas gikan Marso hangtod Mayo, kasagaran ang static shock sa metal! Dili dali bitbiton sa uga nga hangin ang natigom nga karga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a known positively charged object is brought near an electroscope with positive charge, the leaves spread further!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses static electricity and charge detection using an electroscope, but the competency specifically requires investigating static electricity effects using common materials such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons. The card does not involve those materials or the guided investigation described, so it only shares the broad topic of static electricity.

copy.en: When a known positively charged object is brought near an electroscope with positive charge, the leaves spread further! This method tells us if an unknown charge is positive or negative.
copy.tl: Kapag inilapit ang kilalang positibong charged object sa electroscope na may positive charge, mas nagbubukas ang mga dahon! Ginagamit ang paraang ito para malaman kung ang unknown charge ay positibo o negatibo.
copy.bis: Inig-abot sa nahibal-ang positibong kargadong butang sa electroscope nga may positibong karga, mas nagbukas pa ang mga dahon! Kining paagi gigamit aron matukoy kung ang dili nahibal-ang karga positibo ba o negatibo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can remove static charge by 'grounding'!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains grounding as a way to remove static charge, which is a concept within static electricity. However, the competency specifically requires investigating the effects of static electricity using common materials such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons. The card does not involve those materials or an investigation; it only provides a conceptual explanation of discharge via grounding, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: You can remove static charge by 'grounding'! The extra charge flows away into the earth, often through metal, making the object balanced or neutral again.
copy.tl: Maaalis ang static charge sa 'grounding'! Ang sobrang charge ay dumadaloy papunta sa lupa, kadalasan sa metal, kaya nagiging balanse o neutral muli ang bagay.
copy.bis: Matangtang ang static charge pinaagi sa 'grounding'! Ang sobra nga charge moagos ngadto sa yuta, kasagaran sa metal, mao nga mahimong balanse o neutral pag-usab ang butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: preventing static discharge from damaging sensitive microchips
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions static discharge but does not involve investigating effects of static electricity using common materials such as a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons. It only describes a practical anti-static device, so it does not directly support the investigation skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: preventing static discharge from damaging sensitive microchips
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses static discharge and grounding but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it teach safe measures in handling electricity. It is about protecting electronics from static, not about the nature of electric current or general electrical safety.

copy.en: When fixing computers, workers wear an antistatic wrist strap connected to the ground! It keeps their charge level equal to the circuit board, preventing static discharge from damaging sensitive microchips.
copy.tl: Kapag nag-aayos ng computer, nagsusuot ang mga technician ng antistatic wrist strap na nakakabit sa lupa! Pinapanatili nito ang pantay na charge level, pumipigil sa static discharge na makakasira ng microchip.
copy.bis: Kung nag-ayo sa computer, nagsuot ang mga technician ug antistatic wrist strap nga nakakonekta sa yuta! Nagpabilin kini sa parehas nga charge level, nagpugong sa static discharge nga makadaot sa microchip.

copy.bis: Sa mabagay nga panahon sa Pilipinas, dali mahanaw ang static electricity! Ang tubig sa hangin magbitbit sa mga karga gikan sa nawong.

Where is the safest place during a lightning storm?

Go inside a building and avoid standing under a tree!
copy.tl:
Saan pinakaligtas magtago panahon ng kidlat?

Pumasok sa loob ng gusali at iwasan ang pagtayo sa ilalim ng puno!
copy.bis:
Asa pinakaluwas panahon sa kilat?

Mas luwas nga mosulod sa balay ug likayan ang pagtindog ilalom sa kahoy!

copy.en: Opposite charges like positive and negative pull toward each other, but like charges push apart!
copy.tl: Ang magkasalungat na karga (positibo at negatibo) ay nag-aakitan, pero ang magkaparehong karga ay nagtutulakan!
copy.bis: Ang magkasukwahing karga (positibo ug negatibo) magbinira, pero ang managsamang karga magsinikway!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Put lotion on dry skin, use fabric softener in the wash, or touch metal with a key first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons

copy.en:
How can you avoid a surprising spark?

Put lotion on dry skin, use fabric softener in the wash, or touch metal with a key first! These simple tricks help the charge leave gently instead of zapping your finger.
copy.tl:
Paano umiwas sa nakakagulat na spark?

Maglagay ng losyon sa balat, gumamit ng fabric softener sa laba, o hawakan ang metal gamit ang susi! Tumutulong ang mga ito para banayad na umalis ang charge sa halip na kumuryente sa daliri mo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglikay sa makakurat nga spark?

Butangi ug lotion ang panit, gamita ang fabric softener sa labhanan, o hikapa ang metal gamit ang yawe! Motabang kini aron mogawas ang charge sa hinay imbes nga mosakt sa imong tudlo.

copy.tl: Ang static ay nananatili sa isang bagay, samantalang ang kuryente sa wire ay tuloy-tuloy na gumagalaw!
copy.bis: Ang static magpabilin sa usa ka dapit, samtang ang kuryente sa wire padayon nga molihok!

copy.en: Hot steam is lighter than the cooler air around it! Because it's light, it floats upward just like a balloon full of hot air. That's why steam always moves up.
copy.tl: Ang mainit na singaw ay mas magaan kaysa sa malamig na hangin! Dahil magaan ito, umaangat pataas parang lobo na puno ng mainit na hangin. Kaya laging pataas ang singaw.
copy.bis: Ang init nga singaw mas gaan kaysa bugnaw nga hangin! Tungod kay gaan kini, mosaka paibabaw sama sa balloon nga puno sa init nga hangin. Mao nga kanunay mosaka ang singaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why steel ships float using density; it has no connection to measuring distance and time when things move. The competency is about measurement of motion, which is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: Heavy steel ships float because their hollow shape is full of air inside, making the ship's overall density lower than water's!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang mabibigat na barkong bakal dahil hugis-lukong ito at puno ng hangin sa loob, kaya mas mababa ang kabuuang density nito kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis: Ang bug-at nga barkong puthaw molutaw kay lungagon ug puno sa hangin sa sulod, mao nga mas ubos ang kinatibuk-ang density niini kaysa tubig!

copy.en:
Why should you keep your steps written in a notebook?

Keep your written steps in the notebook while you work! A plan only in your head is too easy to accidentally change.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat nakasulat ang mga steps sa notebook?

Panatilihin ang nakasulat na steps sa notebook habang nagtatrabaho! Ang planong nasa isip lang ay madaling mabago nang hindi sinasadya.
copy.bis:
Nganong dapat nakasulat ang mga steps sa notebook?

Tipigi ang nasulat nga steps sa notebook samtang nagbuhat! Ang plano nga naa ra sa huna-huna dali ra usbon nga wala’y tuyo.

Want your sweet drink faster?

Just stir it! Stirring your drink makes the sugar dissolve much faster.
copy.tl:
Gusto mo ng mas mabilis na matamis na inumin?

Kutawin mo lang! Kapag hinahalo o kinukutaw ang inumin, mas mabilis matunaw ang asukal.
copy.bis:
Gusto nimo nga mas paspas nga matam-is ang imong ilimnon?

Kutawa lang! Kon imong kutawon ang ilimnon, mas paspas matunaw ang asukal.

What should you do if your clothes catch fire?

Stop, drop, and roll on the ground! This cuts off oxygen and puts out the flames.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gagawin mo kung nasunog ang damit mo?

Huminto, lumapag, at gumulong sa lupa! Mapuputol nito ang oxygen at mamamatay ang apoy.
copy.bis:
Unsay buhaton nimo kung masunog ang imong sinina?

Hunong, hapa, ug ligid sa yuta! Maputol niini ang oxygen ug mapalong ang kalayo.

copy.en:
How do we measure the height of a storm surge?

It is measured in meters, based on how far the water rises above the normal sea level!
copy.tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang taas ng isang storm surge?

Sinusukat ito sa metro, batay sa kung gaano kataas ang tubig kumpara sa normal na antas ng dagat!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-sukod sa gihabugon sa storm surge?

Gisukod kini sa metro, base sa kon unsa kataas ang tubig kompara sa normal nga lebel sa dagat!

copy.en:
How can one tiny thing destroy so much ozone?

CFC chemicals release chlorine in the stratosphere. One chlorine atom destroys thousands of ozone molecules—it gets used and freed again and again, like a machine that never stops!
copy.tl:
Paano kaya sirain ng isang maliit na bagay ang napakaraming ozone?

Naglalabas ang CFC ng chlorine sa stratosphere. Isang chlorine atom ang sumisira ng libo-libong ozone molecules—ginagamit at pinalaya nang paulit-ulit, parang makina na walang tigil!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagguba sa usa ka gamay nga butang sa daghang ozone?

Ang CFC mubuga og chlorine sa stratosphere. Usa ka chlorine atom makaguba sa liboan ka ozone molecules—gamiton ug buhian balik-balik, sama sa makina nga walay hunong!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The stratosphere sits above the troposphere and holds the ozone layer.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere

copy.en: The stratosphere sits above the troposphere and holds the ozone layer. The air there is calm, which is why jet airplanes fly in it!
copy.tl: Ang stratosphere ay nasa itaas ng troposphere at may ozone layer. Kalmado ang hangin dito kaya lumilipad ang mga jet airplane dito!
copy.bis: Ang stratosphere anaa sa ibabaw sa troposphere ug adunay ozone layer. Kalmado ang hangin dinhi maong manglupad ang mga jet nga ayroplano dinhi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer blocks most of the dangerous UV rays!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why sunburn is delayed (ozone blocking UV) but does not describe any safety measures people can use to avoid harmful effects of the Sun's light. It is background knowledge, not a safety measure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer blocks most of the dangerous UV rays!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the ozone layer and UV rays, which are part of the atmosphere and solar energy, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. It only states a protective effect, not the interaction mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer blocks most of the dangerous UV rays!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any overall characteristics of the Sun such as composition, size, or main energy radiated. It is about the ozone layer's effect on UV radiation, unrelated to the Sun's characteristics.

copy.en:
Why don't we get sunburned right away outside?

The ozone layer blocks most of the dangerous UV rays! Without it, even a short time in the strong sun could badly burn our skin.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi tayo agad napapaso sa labas?

Hinahadlangan ng ozone layer ang karamihan sa mapanganib na UV rays! Kung wala ito, kahit sandali lang sa matinding araw ay maaari nang makapaso ang ating balat.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili dayon kita mapaso sa gawas?

Gibabagan sa ozone layer ang kadaghanan sa peligroso nga UV rays! Kon wala kini, bisan mubo lang sa kusog nga adlaw makapaso na gyud sa atong panit.

copy.en: Another name for a stratovolcano is a composite volcano, because it is built of mixed lava and ash!
copy.tl: Ang ibang tawag sa stratovolcano ay composite volcano, dahil binubuo ito ng pinaghalong lava at abo!
copy.bis: Ang laing ngalan sa stratovolcano mao ang composite volcano, kay gihimo kini sa sagol nga lava ug abo!

copy.en: When sweeping, the broom drags dirt along! This happens because of friction between its bristles and the ground.
copy.tl: Kapag nagwawalis, kinakaladkad ng walis ang basura! Nangyayari ito dahil sa friction o kuskusan sa pagitan ng tinting at lupa.
copy.bis: Kon manilhig, gibira sa silhig ang basura! Mahitabo kini tungod sa friction o panagkuskos tali sa silhig ug sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cortisol from the adrenal glands to raise blood sugar for energy, while adrenaline speeds up your heartbeat

It provides a specific physiological response rather than the concept of homeostasis itself.

copy.en: When you're stressed, your body releases cortisol from the adrenal glands to raise blood sugar for energy, while adrenaline speeds up your heartbeat.
copy.tl: Kapag stressed, naglalabas ang katawan mo ng cortisol mula sa adrenal glands para taasan ang blood sugar bilang enerhiya, habang pinapabilis naman ng adrenaline ang tibok ng puso mo.
copy.bis: Kung ma-stress, ang lawas mopagawas og cortisol gikan sa adrenal glands aron itaas ang blood sugar para sa enerhiya, samtang ang adrenaline mopaspas sa imong pitik sa kasingkasing.
